schema: Each entry maps one real UK Financial Ombudsman Service decision to a scenario over an existing persona policy that models a comparable clause type. The mapping is illustrative: it tests whether the twin surfaces the same clause TYPE a human adjudicator and ombudsman actually argued about, using our own policy's qualifiers (the decision's own numbers are not reproduced, since our persona wordings are not the policies in dispute). This is a small, hand-selected sample, not a statistical estimate of agreement.

mappings.quoted_clause: Any claims due to or arising from any of the following will not be covered: pre-existing medical conditions... excluded, until you have been clear of it for a continuous 24 month period prior to the commencement of claim.
mappings.note: The ombudsman's case turns on a pre-existing-condition exclusion with a clear-period requirement; HI-INDIV-S has a structurally equivalent 24-month pre-existing exclusion (x_preexisting_hospitalization). The decision's own 12/24-month figures are not reused.

mappings.quoted_clause: Existing conditions are excluded for the first 2 years of cover and will only be covered once you have been 2 years, symptom, treatment, medication or consultation free.
mappings.note: This decision's clause is a 2-year pre-existing exclusion that only clears after a symptom-free period; we test it inside the 24-month window (month 6) to check whether the twin surfaces the exclusion-type match. The symptom-free clearance condition itself is not modelled.

mappings.quoted_clause: Means the insured member is incapacitated by an illness or injury so that he is unable to undertake all occupations which we consider appropriate to his experience, training or education.
mappings.note: This decision was classified under our 'waiting_period' regex because the underlying policy defines incapacity with a qualifying-period structure; the underlying dispute is actually about the definition of incapacity, not a waiting period. We keep the entry to show the twin's ground does NOT match in this case, which is an honest negative result of the automatic clause-type classifier, not a successful mapping.
